mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of the Sole Foreign Shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry or equivalent competent registrar in the sole foreign shareholder's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague route: notarize before a local notary in the source jurisdiction and obtain an Apostille from the competent authority of that jurisdiction, then have the document translated into Chinese by a certified PRC translation service, then present to the Chinese market regulation authority. Non-Hague route: notarize before a local notary, authenticate through the source jurisdiction's Ministry of Foreign Affairs, then legalize through the Chinese Embassy or Consulate in the source jurisdiction, then translate into Chinese. Apostille and consular legalization are parallel and mutually exclusive; never chain them sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing of the Sole Foreign Shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry or competent corporate registrar in the sole foreign shareholder's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague route: notarize and Apostille in the source jurisdiction if it is an Apostille Convention state, then translate into Chinese by a certified PRC translator, then present to the Chinese authorities. Non-Hague route: notarize, authenticate with the source country Ministry of Foreign Affairs, legalize at the Chinese Embassy or Consulate in that source country, then translate into Chinese. Apostille and consular legalization are parallel and mutually exclusive; never chain them sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution Resolving Incorporation of the WFOE and Appointing the Legal Representative and Authorized Signatories, together with Power of Attorney

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague route: certify the board resolution before a notary, obtain an Apostille from the competent authority of the source state, translate into Chinese by a certified PRC translator, and file with SAMR. Non-Hague route: certify before a notary, authenticate through the source state's Ministry of Foreign Affairs, legalize through the Chinese Embassy or Consulate in that state, and translate into Chinese. Apostille and consular legalization are parallel and mutually exclusive; never chain them sequentially.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all shareholders, UBOs holding 25% or more, directors, legal representatives, supervisors, senior managers and authorized signatories at the time of incorporation and periodically thereafter. Screening covers global politically exposed persons (PEP) lists, OFAC SDN and non-SDN lists, UN Security Council Consolidated List, EU and UK consolidated financial sanctions, China's Unreliable Entity List, MOFCOM export control entity lists, domestic criminal enforcement lists, and any other applicable Chinese AML/CFT watchlists. Automated live screening must be supplemented by manual review, adverse media checks, source-of-funds verification and enhanced due diligence if any risk flag arises. Results must be documented and retained for anti-money laundering audit purposes.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) Enterprise Name Self-Declaration System, accessible through the National Integrated Online Government Service Platform and local municipal SAMR name pre-registration portals
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The statutory registered name of a Chinese WFOE must be in Chinese characters and follow the four-tier naming convention: administrative division plus distinctive trade name plus industry or operating characteristic plus legal form. For a WFOE manufacturing industrial edge computing products, the industry tier must reflect the permitted business scope, such as industrial computer manufacturing or computer numerical control equipment manufacturing. The foreign shareholder's name may be transliterated phonetically into Chinese characters; pinyin alone is not sufficient for official registration. Foreign-script words are not permitted as the statutory Chinese corporate name. The English name is optional and does not replace the Chinese statutory name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the proposed WFOE name is rejected, the applicant may apply for administrative reconsideration with the next higher SAMR authority or the same-level people's government within 60 days from the date of receipt of the written rejection decision. The appeal must include the proposed Chinese name, the rejection notice number, the statutory basis for permissibility under the Enterprise Name Registration Regulations, and evidence that the name does not create confusion with any existing enterprise. Alternatively, or after administrative reconsideration, the applicant may file an administrative lawsuit with the competent people's court within six months. The name reservation may be extended once for an additional 180 days by filing a timely extension application before expiry, and if the reservation expires the applicant must file a new name declaration.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: For this industrial manufacturing WFOE, a virtual office or commercial mailbox is not acceptable as a statutory registered address. Local SAMR, tax authorities and banks require a physical address evidenced by a valid property ownership certificate or a registered lease agreement. A postal-only mailbox cannot demonstrate commercial substance for a business manufacturing rugged industrial computers and edge gateways, and is likely to trigger refusal by banks opening corporate accounts, rejection during tax registration, and administrative penalties for falsifying registered address. A physical industrial office and production facility must be procured and maintained.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Unannounced inspection checklist: registered address signage and physical office existence, lease contract and property ownership certificate availability, presence of production machinery and inventory, number of employees and social insurance records, utility and rent invoices, bank account activity and tax declarations, and consistency between the business license scope and actual edge computing product manufacturing. Quantified risk: moderate; approximately 40% annual probability of municipal tax authority site verification and 25% annual probability of SAMR address compliance inspection for manufacturing WFOEs. The risk rises to approximately 70% if a virtual office or registered-address mismatch is detected.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Company Law of the People's Republic of China (2023 Revision, effective 1 July 2024), Articles 23-29 on incorporation and Articles 36-41 on corporate governance; Foreign Investment Law of the People's Republic of China (2019), Articles 2, 4, 6 and the Special Administrative Measures for Foreign Investment Access (Negative List) 2021; Regulations on the Administration of Market Entities Registration (State Council Order No. 746), Articles 8-10 and 16-21; Company Registration Measures of the State Administration for Market Regulation.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Local Administration for Market Regulation (AMR) of the city/district where the WFOE is domiciled, operating under the national supervision of the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR). Registrations are processed through the SAMR Integrated Enterprise Registration Online System and the local Government Affairs Service Hall.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Establishment Registration of a Company together with the Articles of Association of [CN] WFOE LTD, filed in the Unified Social Credit Code registration system and evidenced by the issuance of a Business License.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum registered capital and no blocked escrow account requirement for a Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise under the revised PRC Company Law and Foreign Investment Law. The registered capital is set by the shareholders in the Articles of Association and must be fully subscribed in cash or kind; under Article 47 of the Company Law (2023), subscribed capital must be paid in full within five years from establishment unless a special industry law provides otherwise. Paid-in contributions must be remitted into the WFOE's licensed RMB or foreign currency capital account in China and verified by the bank; no regulatory escrow arrangement is imposed. The foreign investor may contribute in USD or another freely convertible currency, and SAFE foreign exchange recordal is completed through the receiving bank.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration of the People's Republic of China (STA), operating through the nationwide electronic tax service platform (e-Tax Bureau) and local competent tax offices.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Foreign Wholly-Owned Enterprise (WFOE) is automatically registered for tax purposes upon incorporation, obtaining a Unified Social Credit Code (USCC) from the Administration for Market Regulation, which also serves as the statutory tax identification number (TIN/VAT identification) and is synchronized to the STA. The WFOE must then complete tax registration particulars in the STA electronic tax service platform within 30 days of the business license issuance, including confirmation of VAT general taxpayer status, enterprise income tax filing basis, payroll withholding registration, and bank account reporting. For a foreign non-resident enterprise without a permanent establishment, tax registration must be obtained through the competent STA office using the statutory non-resident tax registration procedure, under which the non-resident enterprise receives a separate tax identification number for fulfillment of China-source withholding tax obligations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. Chinese tax law does not provide check-the-box or entity classification elections for a WFOE. A WFOE is mandatorily taxed as a resident enterprise under the Enterprise Income Tax Law. Treaty benefits are applied through filing and documentation rather than elective classification; hybrid mismatch rules are not elective.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: RMB 5,000,000 annual taxable sales, which is the mandatory threshold for VAT general taxpayer registration; all VAT taxpayers must register with the STA, but those below the threshold are classified as small-scale taxpayers under the simplified method.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: The STA operates the National Electronic Invoice Service Platform. VAT invoices must be issued through STA-certified tax-control systems and fully digitalized electronic invoices are reported in real-time to the platform, which assigns a unique anti-fraud invoice number, dynamic QR code, and digital stamping before the invoice is valid for tax credit or export refund purposes. API-based integration is mandatory for high-volume issuers.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Export sales of goods physically shipped out of China qualify for the 0% VAT rate provided the WFOE is a VAT general taxpayer, the goods are actually exported with customs clearance, the export proceeds are repatriated in foreign exchange within the statutory deadline, and the transaction is fully documented. Qualifying offshore services rendered to overseas clients may also be zero-rated under applicable Ministry of Finance and STA regulations. Domestic sales of rugged industrial computers and edge gateways are taxable at 13%.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Goods Declaration (export bill of entry)
Bill of Lading or equivalent multimodal transport document
Commercial invoice and foreign sales contract
VAT special invoice or export invoice reflecting zero-rating
Bank foreign exchange receipt certificate or SAFE-verified export proceeds record
Export tax refund/zero-rating declaration and reconciliation ledger
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: If the STA determines that zero-rating was claimed without actual export, without verified foreign exchange repatriation, or based on false documentation, the refund is disallowed and clawed back with late-payment surcharge of 0.05% per day from the due date. Fraudulent export refund claims are penalized at one to five times the refunded amount under Article 66 of the Tax Administration and Collection Law, with criminal liability for export tax fraud, suspension of export tax refund qualification, and inclusion in the tax non-compliance blacklist.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: People's Bank of China (PBoC) and State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: China maintains a guarded capital account with full convertibility on the current account for bona fide trade and service transactions under the Foreign Exchange Administration Regulations. RMB is convertible for current-account transactions, but capital-account transactions require entity-level registration at SAFE, including foreign debt filing, direct investment registration, and capital account opening. For a WFOE, the paid-in capital injection is treated as foreign direct investment and must be registered with SAFE before wiring; subsequent profit remittance requires submission of audited financial statements, corporate income tax filing proof, and a SAFE-registered bank's verification of the same. Export proceeds are repatriated to the entity's domestic foreign exchange account and may be kept as foreign currency or settled to CNY at the entity's discretion. The practical hurdles to full capital outflow include the requirement to prove the commercial genuineness of each outward remittance, maintain at least a 5-year retention of trade documents, and observe NDRC and MOFCOM reporting thresholds for cross-border transaction flows. Accordingly, currency convertibility is legally open on the current account but functionally constrained by SAFE monitoring and purpose-code verification on the capital account.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export foreign currency receipts must be fully repatriated into the WFOE's domestic designated foreign exchange account and verified against the Customs export declaration via the SAFE trade monitoring system within 30 calendar days. The statutory mandatory conversion ratio is effectively 0%, i.e. no forced surrender into CNY; settlement into RMB is voluntary and can be executed at any time, but any non-settlement in foreign currency requires continuous foreign exchange income reporting to the central bank.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low. Fintech electronic money institutions such as Wise, Revolut, or Payoneer are not licensed by the PBoC to provide banking services or maintain onshore clearing accounts for corporates in mainland China. A WFOE cannot rely on an offshore EMI as its primary treasury interface because local FX settlement and capital account receipts must flow through a SAFE-designated domestic bank. Offshore EMIs can only function as a supplementary collection/outreach corridor for small values, and only where the underlying payment is not a capital-account transaction; even then, the WFOE's legal books and tax filings will require full transparency of any offsetting transaction.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence in-branch is effectively mandatory for the WFOE's statutory director and the primary signatory at account opening. Mainland banks do not accept a remote consular proxy opening for a newly established WFOE unless the opening is handled through a mainland legal representative holding a notarized power of attorney executed under Chinese law and evidenced by a mainland notary public. In special cases, Bank of China permits an interview by live video conference for the beneficial owner if the entity holds valid corporate registration documents and the branch's AML officer pre-clears the risk file; however all documentary originals must still be couriered and verified by a branch manager before account activation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Layered and opaque beneficial ownership chain regarding the offshore parent entity, especially if the parent is an anonymous holding company in a high-secrecy jurisdiction.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Organizational corporate tree signed and sealed by the parent directors, an audited cap table, notarized shareholder registers, a full UBO declaration with passport copies and proof of residential address, a legal opinion from the parent jurisdiction qualified counsel, and an auditor's confirmation that no nominee shareholding or bearer shares exist.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Undeclared dual-use exposure of industrial edge computing appliances subject to Chinese export control or foreign re-export licensing, triggering anti-proliferation review.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Product technical specification with Chinese customs classification and HS code, MOFCOM-NDRC export control product self-checklist, signed end-user certificate and end-use undertaking from the overseas buyer, independent engineering assessment confirming no military or nuclear utility, and a copy of the General Administration of Customs export registration.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade route and payment token anomalies in the outbound disbursement plan, including contracts with high-risk dealer countries or wiring to private bank accounts of intermediaries rather than direct suppliers.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Vendor justification memo, original commercial invoice referencing shipment terms, packing list with container-level item description, original marine bill of lading and air waybill where applicable, customs export declaration forms, and a wire transfer-pool report showing that the contract counterparty matches the receiving bank and payee identity exactly.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Capital injection volume at formation sprinting beyond the business scale declared in the business plan, raising suspicion of round-tripping.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Forward-looking business plan vetted by the board, 24-month projected hiring and revenue curve, lease and employment agreements for the industrial facility, a certified capital verification report from a licensed Chinese public accountant, and SAFE Foreign Investment Registration proof evidencing the original foreign exchange source of the capital.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All inbound FDI capital contributions for the WFOE must be routed through a designated domestic bank via SWIFT MT103 wire, referencing the unique SAFE Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) Code and an invoice paying purpose code classified as 'Equity Capital Contribution - foreign direct investment remittance'. The bank performs a pre-credit check against the SAFE registration file; the funds are temporarily booked to a suspense account and cannot be used until the accountant issues a formal capital verification report and the local branch completes the foreign currency capital settlement. Only after such verification may the funds be transferred to the WFOE's operating RMB account and disbursed according to the board-approved cash flow.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade disbursements for production inputs are cleared through the SWIFT MT103 network for T/T settlements, MT700 for commercial LCs where suppliers require a bank undertaking, and SWIFT MT400 for documentary collection against presentation of shipping documents; all outbound wires require an official supplier invoice, proof of customs registration where applicable, and must be reported into the SAFE trade receipts and payments system for verification against the original import declaration.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore RMB/USD and RMB/EUR deliverable forwards available only through PBoC- and SAFE-licensed banks, backed by genuine trade exposure with a maximum tenor of 12 months.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are not permitted within the onshore Chinese market for domestic-licensed entities; WFOEs are restricted from executing NDFs in the domestic balance sheet unless booked through offshore subsidiary accounts under a separate SAFE case-by-case approval.

Cross-currency swaps are permissible only where the underlying risk is a real converted capital or trade-flow currency requirement, and the transaction must be registered in the bank's counterparty credit and SAFE's derivative trade reporting system.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Enterprise Credit Information Publicity Report (Company Annual Report to the State Administration for Market Regulation)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) - National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 1 January to 30 June of the year following each fiscal year-end; reporting information as at 31 December of the prior year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to publish within the window places the company on the Operating Abnormal List; if unrectified for three consecutive years, transfer to the Serious Illegal and Untrustworthy Enterprise List triggers credit constraints, legal representative restrictions, and prospective administrative strike-off or business license revocation by the registration authority.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Foreign Investment Information Report (Foreign Investment Law annual reporting scheme)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM) and local commerce departments; submitted jointly through the SAMR annual report portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 1 January to 30 June of the year following each fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Rectification orders, administrative fines under the Foreign Investment Law reporting regime, inclusion in the joint credit information system, and suspension risk for future investment-license, capital-change, or cross-border payment procedures.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Final Settlement and Filing Return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) - local competent tax authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually no later than 31 May of the year following the tax year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of RMB 2,000 to RMB 10,000 or higher for serious non-compliance; daily late-payment surcharge of 0.05% of unpaid tax; understatement penalty ranging from 50% to 500% of the tax shortfall; persistent failure may result in enforced tax collection, credit rating downgrade, and frozen tax-filing functionalities.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Statutory Annual Financial Report Audit by an Independent Certified Public Accountant
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Independent licensed PRC accounting firm; audit report delivered to the shareholders' meeting and retained for on-site inspection by SAMR, STA, and State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual audit to be completed within six months after fiscal year-end and before the regular shareholders' meeting, using 31 December as the statutory balance-sheet date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No government filing fee; failure to obtain an audit may trigger shareholders' actions and articles-of-association defaults, refusal by SAFE of dividend or capital repatriation, higher tax/customs inspection ratio, and administrative examination under the PRC Accounting Law.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial Ownership and Shareholding Transfer Information Filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: SAMR Beneficial Ownership Information Management System with People's Bank of China (PBOC) data sharing; administered via local market regulation branches
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 calendar days after incorporation, after any beneficial ownership change, or after each shareholding transfer; annual confirmation embedded in the SAMR annual report due 30 June
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Rectification order, administrative fines for late or inaccurate UBO filings, adverse credit annotations, and suspension of subsequent registration or tax-de-registration applications until the filing is cured.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Industrial Statistical Declaration (industrial-edge manufacturing unit)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Bureau of Statistics (NBS) - local statistics bureau / industrial statistics division
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually not later than 31 March following the reporting year, or the earlier date directed by the municipal statistics bureau
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Rectification notices, fines under the Statistics Law, inclusion in statistical credit record, and coordinated restrictions on government subsidy and credit-incentive applications for repeated violations.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under PRC Company Law Article 164 and PRC Accounting Law Article 20, every limited liability company, including a wholly foreign-owned enterprise, must undergo an annual independent audit by a licensed CPA firm; there is no balance-sheet, turnover, or headcount de-minimis exemption for a WFOE. Quantitative size thresholds only become relevant for special regulated/public-interest entities applying CSRC, SASAC, or NFRA audit rules; for a private WFOE, the legal trigger is entity type rather than size.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: PRC Accounting Standards for Business Enterprises (ASBE / China GAAP), substantially IFRS-consistent; eligible small-scale entities may adopt the simplified Standards for Small Enterprises under Ministry of Finance rules; cross-border reporting may include IFRS reconciliation for foreign-parent consolidation, with statutory books maintained in RMB.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The Beneficial Ownership Information Management Measures impose a 30-calendar-day reporting window from the occurrence of any shareholding transfer, equity change, or beneficial ownership change, and also require initial UBO filing at incorporation. No standalone annual UBO return is issued; instead the SAMR annual report (due 30 June) acts as the annual confirmation and exposes any divergence between registered shareholders, UBO data, and audited equity structure. Share transfers must be recorded in the statutory shareholders register and filed with SAMR before the UBO update can be processed.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Charges/Mortgages and Equity Pledges
Shareholder Transfer Ledger and 30-Day UBO Change Log

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: $500-$1,500 per year for a registered office address and standard statutory filing agent; $1,200-$2,800 per year in tier-1 cities with full corporate-secretarial and countersigning support
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: $1,800-$4,500 for a small WFOE with straightforward books; $4,000-$10,000 for an industrial edge-computing manufacturer with fixed assets, inventory, and cross-border revenue streams

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% under PRC Enterprise Income Tax Law Article 4; resident enterprises (including WFOEs) are taxed on worldwide income. Non-resident enterprises without a permanent establishment are taxed at 10% on China-source dividends, interest, royalties, and rentals, subject to tax treaty relief.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: A qualifying High/New-technology Enterprise (HNTE) may apply a 15% concessional rate; qualifying Small Low-Profit Enterprises benefit from preferential reduced rates on taxable income up to RMB 3 million; software/IC enterprises may enjoy two-year exemption and three-year 50% reduction regimes; certain encouraged manufacturing industries in the western regions may benefit from a 15% rate; R&D expenses are generally additionally deductible at 100% (super deduction) for qualified industries.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: PRC Enterprise Income Tax Annual Return Form A100000 (A Class) with supporting schedules (Form A000000 basic information table, A102010, A102020, A105000 adjustment series, A107010 tax exemption/reduction series, A108000 foreign tax credit schedule); electronic filing through the State Taxation Administration Electronic Tax Bureau (e-Tax) portal using digital certification.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual statutory return; quarterly or monthly provisional enterprise income tax prepayments during the year.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Quarterly prepayments: within 15 days after the close of each quarter or month. Annual return: within five months after the fiscal year-end. A calendar-year WFOE must file the final annual return and settle by 31 May of the following year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 1 / Form A100000 Line 1 - Total operating revenue (sales of goods, services, and other business revenue)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter gross revenue from manufacture and sale of rugged industrial computers, edge gateways, embedded systems, and related after-sales services; include all related-party export sales at transfer-priced arm's length amounts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report all turnover earned by the China-incorporated WFOE, including export sales to the foreign parent group. Reconcile revenue with customs export declarations, VAT export invoices, and intercompany agreements. Understating revenue to shift profit offshore is a fatal transfer-pricing red flag.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2 / Form A100000 Line 2 - Cost of operations (operating cost)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter direct materials, direct labor, manufacturing overheads, depreciation, and production-related costs attributable to the industrial computing product lines.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deduct only actual, documented costs supported by purchase contracts, customs records, VAT invoices, and warehouse movement records. Related-party raw material purchases must satisfy the arm's length standard and be substantiated in the China Local File; inflated or circular intercompany purchases create false deduction exposure.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 3 / Form A100000 Line 3 - Gross profit / gross margin
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Box 3 is derived by subtracting the cost of operations from operating revenue; this line is cross-checked against industry gross margins and BEPS-derived economic substance expectations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the WFOE performs core manufacturing, logistics, quality assurance, and warranty activities, the gross margin should reflect those functions, assets, and risks. A margin that is inexplicably compressed while the foreign parent earns large residual profits will trigger a transfer pricing examination.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 4 / Form A100000 Line 4 - Selling, general, and administrative expenses, plus finance costs
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter period expenses: marketing, technical support, management fees, research and development costs, loan interest, exchange losses, and other administrative expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Management fees paid to a foreign parent are deductible only if the parent actually performs specific services and supports the fee with invoices, contracts, and service reports; pure allocation of global overhead is non-deductible and must be disallowed. Interest paid on intercompany loans in excess of arm's length debt/equity ratios (thin capitalization) is non-deductible and subject to withholding on the actual payment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 / Form A100000 Lines 5-10 - Operating profit, profit total, and reconciliation to taxable income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: These lines set out operating profit, non-operating income/expenses, and accounting profit on the audited financial statements before tax adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A WFOE must crosswalk its statutory financial statements to the CIT return. Non-resident investors examine the consistency with the group's audited consolidation and the intercompany transfer pricing policies; any unreported valuation gains, early payments, or forgiven loans are added back.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 6 / Form A100000 Lines 11-14 - Tax adjustments: add-backs, deductible items, and tax loss carryforward
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter permanent and temporary differences, including disallowed expenses, non-taxable income, deductible R&D super-deductions, and loss carryforwards.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the statutory five-year loss carryforward rule (or ten-year rule for qualified HNTE and technology-oriented SMEs). Losses must be supported by the WFOE's own tax records; transfer of losses from the foreign group is prohibited. Any adjustment proposed by SAT in a transfer pricing audit must be booked accordingly.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 7 / Form A100000 Line 15 - Taxable income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report the final taxable amount after all adjustments, deductions, exemptions, and loss carryforwards; apply the applicable tax rate in the following line.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a WFOE claiming the 15% HNTE rate, ensure the valid HNTE certificate, core IP ownership, and CIGA in China are present. If the foreign parent retains key IP or the manufacturing entity lacks technological novelty, the reduced rate may be reversed with retroactive interest.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 8 / Form A100000 Lines 16-22 - Tax payable, tax credits, foreign tax credit, and final CIT settlement
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Compute the current-year tax, apply domestic preferential incentives and the foreign tax credit for foreign-source income, and determine the net tax payable or overpayment.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For outbound dividend distributions, the WFOE or its agent must withhold 10% non-resident enterprise income tax unless a reduced DTA rate applies and the beneficial owner/Tax Residency Certificate documentation has been submitted before the payment date. Simultaneously report the distribution in the annual return and the withholding tax remittance form.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 9 / Schedules and charts - Related-party transactions schedule (Form A105000/ related party tables)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclose all related-party transactions, including sales, purchases, loans, royalties, and service fees, in the annual filing package if the materiality thresholds are met.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A WFOE exporting industrial computing products to its foreign parent must complete the related-party transaction tables and contemporaneous TP documentation. In an audit, missing documentation invites penalties and a discretionary reallocation of income under the unilateral/contribution and profit-split rules.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of the annual enterprise income tax return attracts a penalty under Article 62 of the PRC Tax Collection and Administration Law (TCAL): RMB 2,000 to RMB 10,000, or RMB 10,000 to RMB 50,000 for serious cases. Under Article 32, overdue tax carries a daily surcharge of 0.05% of the unpaid tax for each day from the statutory deadline. Under Article 63, the refusal to file or fraudulent understatement of tax results in recovery of the underpaid tax plus a monetary penalty ranging from 50% to 500% of the unpaid tax; in serious cases criminal prosecution under Criminal Law Article 201 may lead to imprisonment for up to seven years and fines. A withholding agent that fails to withhold and remit tax is subject to penalty under Article 69 (typically 50% to 300% of the un-withheld tax amount, plus restoration obligations).

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% on dividends distributed by the China-resident WFOE to a non-resident corporate shareholder, imposed under Article 3(3) and Article 4(2) of the PRC Enterprise Income Tax Law and Articles 37/38 of the Detailed Implementation Regulations. No withholding applies to dividends paid to another resident enterprise; DTA reductions may apply to non-resident shareholders.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To benefit from a reduced dividend/interest/royalty rate under the applicable Double Taxation Agreement or Arrangement, the non-resident recipient must: (1) obtain a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from its home-country tax authority, generally covering the calendar year of payment; (2) complete and submit the Chinese Treaty Benefit Application Form (including the Beneficial Owner Self-Declaration) to the WFOE or the competent SAT office through the electronic tax bureau before making the cross-border payment; (3) provide documentary evidence of beneficial ownership, supported by board resolutions, bank statements, substance-related employment/personnel, records of economic activity, and a statement that the income is not derived through a shell or conduit; (4) disclose whether the non-resident has a permanent establishment or fixed base in China, because if such presence exists the dividend/interest/royalty will be taxed on a net basis as business income; and (5) ensure the reduced rate is reflected in the tax certificate or remittance form, and if already over-withheld, apply for a refund under Article 51 of TCAL within the applicable statute of limitations.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: The statutory withholding rates for non-resident recipients are 10% for interest and 10% for royalties, plus VAT and possible local surcharges. Under a favorable DTA, the treaty rates vary: interest may be reduced to 0%, 5%, or 7% for financial institutions if the recipient is the beneficial owner and the debt is arm's length; royalties generally range from 5% to 10%, with industrial, commercial, or scientific equipment royalties sometimes 5-7%; rate reductions are denied if the recipient is a conduit without beneficial ownership or if the payer is a branch being characterized as a permanent establishment.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File: required for a China resident taxpayer if, in the preceding taxable year, any of the following related-party transaction thresholds is exceeded - tangible property transactions above RMB 200 million; financial asset transactions above RMB 100 million; intangible property transactions above RMB 20 million; or other related-party transactions above RMB 40 million. Master File: required where the total aggregate amount of related-party transactions of the consolidated group exceeds RMB 1 billion, or where the enterprise is selected or instructed by the SAT to prepare it.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Mainland China does not operate a standalone Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) code in the style of offshore financial centers; nevertheless, the PRC Enterprise Income Tax Law applies substance-over-form and general anti-avoidance under Article 47, and SAT notices on treaty benefit entitlement require the beneficial owner to conduct real economic activity. A WFOE manufacturing rugged industrial computers and edge gateways must demonstrate that its personnel, factories, inventory, pricing decisions, risk management, research if applicable, and core income-generating activities (CIGA) physically and strategically reside in China; a shell that merely signs contracts and invoices while the parent controls all economics will be recharacterized and denied treaty benefits.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax evasion through fabricated cost deductions and false VAT invoices
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The WFOE uses artificially issued retail/commercial invoices, sham service agreements, or inflated procurement contracts from related or third-party suppliers to increase deductible costs, depress taxable profit, shift profit out of China, or obtain excess VAT export rebates.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Violates Article 8 of the EIT Law, Articles 21(2) and 63 of the PRC Tax Collection and Administration Law, and Article 204/205 of the PRC Criminal Law (crime of making falsely issued special VAT invoices and crime of evading tax/export tax refund fraud). Financial penalty: recovery of tax underpaid plus 50% to 500% penalty; daily late-payment surcharge at 0.05%; criminal fines up to the amount of evaded tax; imprisonment up to 7 years for tax evasion; up to 10 years for export tax refund fraud.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Courts and tax authorities may pierce the corporate veil under the PRC Company Law and TCAL implementation rules: the director/legal representative who signs tax returns or directs false invoicing is jointly and severally liable for the corporate tax debt with personal assets; personal bank accounts may be frozen (asset preservation); a heftier travel restriction is imposed through the High Court enforcement blacklist ('restricted high-consumption list'), including prohibition on overseas air/high-speed rail travel; criminal liability attaches personally, including detention and imprisonment, especially when the legal representative orders or acquiesces in the false invoicing.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell company structure with no economic substance and treaty shopping for reduced withholding
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The foreign shareholder (or an intermediary holding company in a tax haven) is added to the corporate chain solely to obtain a reduced dividend/interest/royalty withholding rate under a DTA. The Chinese WFOE does not engage in actual substantive business activity; the offshore intermediary has no personnel or economic function other than receiving distributions, and all management is dictated from the true parent country.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty benefits under the PRC EIT Law Article 47, the general anti-avoidance rule, and the Beneficial Ownership Notice (SAT Announcement 2018 No. 9). The tax authority may recharacterize the transaction, refuse the reduced rate, impose the full statutory 10% withholding plus late-payment surcharge, and assess penalties between 50% and 500% of the tax underpaid.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: A director who causes the WFOE to execute artificial conduit contracts or to facilitate treaty-benefit fraud may be held civilly liable for restitution of the unpaid withholding tax; the competent tax court may order freezing of personal savings, shares, and real estate; an asset preservation order may extend to overseas enforcement under China's international asset-sharing mechanisms; the individual may be subject to a travel ban and placed on the tax-integrity blacklist; in cases of malicious false beneficial-ownership declarations, criminal tax evasion liability may be pursued.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Undervalued export invoices and profit shifting in related-party industrial computer exports
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The WFOE sells rugged industrial computers and edge gateways to its foreign parent at controlled prices that do not reflect the actual functions, risks, and intangibles contributed by the Chinese entity; the export price is deliberately low so that profit accumulates abroad, and the customs declaration value is understated to manipulate VAT export refund computations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Contravenes the arm's length principle under EIT Law Article 41 and the Special Tax Adjustment Implementation Measures (SAT Order No. 6 and SAT Announcement 2016 No. 42); Customs Law and VAT export refund regulations characterize the under-valuation as false declaration; penalty includes customs fines of up to three times the undeclared duty, VAT export refund clawback, and under TCAL Article 64 a 50-500% penalty on the transferred profit; criminal liability for false export/receiving export tax refunds under Criminal Law Article 204 can lead to imprisonment up to 10 years or more for large amounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly sign low-priced transfer pricing invoices or instruct the misdeclaration of customs values render the corporate veil pierceable: they are jointly liable for the incremental taxes, customs duties, and export refunds wrongfully obtained; personal assets can be attached by the tax and customs authorities; the director's exit visa is cancelled/blocked by the court; where deliberate evasion exceeds statutory thresholds, imprisonment for up to ten years may be applied, in addition to monetary fines and confiscation of personal gains.
